cli.help: Generate, manage and run browser automation scenarios.
cli.lang.help: Interface language. Defaults to {default}; can also be set with the {env} environment variable.
cli.lang.invalid: {value} is not a supported language. Choose from {choices}.
cli.validate.help: Validate scenario files and point to the file, line, step and field of each problem. Accepts files or directories; a directory is searched for all .yaml and .yml files. Exits with 0 when everything passes, otherwise 1.
cli.validate.format_help: Output format: text for people, json for programs and AI.
cli.schema.help: Print the JSON Schema of the scenario DSL, for editor autocompletion, AI generation and the frontend. With a scenario file, print the JSON Schema of that scenario's inputs or outputs instead.
cli.schema.short_help: Print the JSON Schema of the scenario DSL.
cli.schema.part_help: Which part to print for a scenario file: inputs or outputs.
cli.run.help: Run a scenario: validate inputs → run the steps in a browser → independent assertions → publish outputs. Each run creates a directory in the output folder with input.json, facts.json, output.json (only when it passes), screenshots, logs and report.html. Exits with 0 when everything passes, otherwise 1.
cli.run.input_value_help: One input, converted to its declared type; may be repeated. Takes precedence over --input.
cli.run.input_file_help: A JSON file of inputs, for example the previous scenario's output.json.
cli.run.input_file_invalid: The input file must contain a JSON object.
cli.run.input_value_invalid: {value} is not in the NAME=VALUE form.
cli.run.base_url_help: Use this URL instead of the scenario's browser.baseUrl, for example a test environment.
cli.run.browser_help: Use this browser instead of the scenario's browser.engine.
cli.run.deadline_help: Overall deadline in milliseconds, instead of the scenario's deadline.
cli.run.out_help: Folder to put run directories in.
cli.run.format_help: Output format: text for people, json for the full result.json.
cli.serve.help: Start the management portal to create, validate, publish and run scenarios and view reports in a browser. Data (SQLite, scenario revisions, run folders) is kept in the --data folder, by default RPA_DATA_DIR or data/. There is no sign-in, so by default only this computer can connect.
cli.serve.host_help: Address to listen on. There is no sign-in; only open it to other computers on a trusted network.
cli.serve.port_help: Port to listen on. Without it, {first} is used; if another program has it, the next free port up to {last}.
cli.serve.data_help: Data folder; defaults to the RPA_DATA_DIR environment variable or data/.
cli.serve.exposed: Warning: {host} is not a loopback address and the portal has no sign-in; anyone on the same network can use it.
cli.serve.started: Management portal: {url} (data: {data}; press Ctrl+C to stop)
cli.serve.port_switched: Port {busy} is used by another program; using {port} instead.
cli.serve.port_busy: Port {port} is used by another program; choose another one, for example --port {suggestion}. To see which program: on macOS or Linux run lsof -nP -iTCP:{port} -sTCP:LISTEN; on Windows run netstat -ano | findstr :{port}.
cli.serve.no_free_port: Ports {first}–{last} are all used by other programs; choose a port with --port.
cli.serve.already_running: The management portal is already running at {url} (probably started earlier and still open); just open that address. To run another one, stop it first, or use --port for another port and --data for another folder.
cli.serve.testsite_help: Also start the local test site (http://127.0.0.1:{port}/); the “Test site automation” cases run against it.
cli.serve.testsite_running: The test site is already running at {url}; using it.
cli.serve.testsite_busy: Port {port} is used by another program, so the test site was not started and the “Test site automation” cases cannot reach it. Stop that program and restart, or add --no-testsite to skip the test site.
cli.serve.browsers_missing: {browsers} not yet downloaded on this computer; scenes that use them will fail. Run {command} in the project folder; no need to restart the Portal.
cli.record.help: Record browser actions on this computer (Playwright codegen): a browser window and the Playwright Inspector open here; close the window when you are done. The recording is saved as Python with passwords masked (--out); add --scenario to also convert it into a scenario DSL draft: typed values become inputs, password fields become secrets, and lines that cannot be converted are kept as comments. Drafts must be validated before publishing.
cli.record.short_help: Record actions into a scenario draft.
cli.record.url_required: Give a start URL, or use --from to convert an existing recording.
cli.record.out_help: Where to save the recording with passwords masked.
cli.record.storage_help: Load this login state (storageState) before recording, e.g. a role's state.json.
cli.record.scenario_help: Also write the converted DSL draft to this file.
cli.record.id_help: Scenario id of the draft; defaults to the name of --out.
cli.record.name_help: Scenario name of the draft; defaults to the id.
cli.record.from_help: Do not record; convert this existing codegen recording.
cli.record.started: Opened {browser} and the Playwright Inspector: close the browser window when you are done.
cli.record.failed: Nothing was recorded (codegen exit code {code}). Computers without a display cannot record; record on a computer with a desktop.
cli.record.secrets: Password fields became secrets: {names} (set their values in the Portal or as environment variables before running)
cli.record.scenario: Scenario draft: {path} (check it with rpa validate; publish only after validation)
cli.run.storage_state_help: For scenarios with login: load this login state file (storageState, e.g. roles/<role>/state.json in the Portal's data folder); it is only loaded, not checked.
cli.serve.worker_port_help: Open a separate external port for devices (for example 8081). It only serves the Worker API and pairing, and every request needs a token or an invitation; the portal pages stay on --host only.
cli.serve.worker_host_help: Address the external port listens on; by default all network interfaces, so devices on the LAN can reach it.
cli.serve.local_worker_help: Also run jobs on this computer (default). With --no-local-worker every job goes to remote workers.
cli.serve.worker_port_same: --worker-port {port} is the same as the portal's port; choose another one.
cli.serve.worker_api: External port: {url} (create an invitation on the portal's Devices page and paste it on that computer; this port only serves the Worker API and pairing. The first time, the operating system may ask whether to allow incoming connections; allow them.)
cli.serve.local_worker_off: This computer does not run jobs (--no-local-worker): every job goes to remote workers.
cli.worker.help: Act as a remote worker on this computer: claim jobs from the management portal, run them in a subprocess and send the reports and artifacts back. Headed browser windows appear on this computer. The first time, pair with an invitation from the portal's Devices page (--invite); after that, just run it. You can also put a token in the {env} environment variable or in the file given with --token-file.
cli.worker.short_help: Act as a remote worker on this computer.
cli.worker.server_help: URL of the portal's external port, for example http://192.168.1.10:8081; not needed after pairing with an invitation.
cli.worker.token_file_help: Read the token from this file; without it, the {env} environment variable is used.
cli.worker.name_help: Display name; defaults to the computer name.
cli.worker.work_dir_help: Working folder for job files and run directories (deleted after upload).
cli.worker.keep_runs_help: Keep the run directories on this computer after uploading them (for troubleshooting).
cli.worker.testsite_help: Also start the local test site (http://127.0.0.1:{port}/); the example scenarios run against it.
cli.worker.no_token: A token is required: paste an invitation from the portal's Devices page with --invite, or set the {env} environment variable, or point --token-file at a file containing the token.
cli.worker.no_display: This computer has no graphical display; it only claims headless jobs.
cli.worker.started: Remote worker “{name}” started: portal {server}, working folder {work}. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
cli.worker.stopping: Stopping: the running job is cancelled and its result reported…
cli.worker.rejected: The portal does not accept this worker: {message}
cli.worker.event_online: Connected to the portal (worker {worker}); waiting for jobs.
cli.worker.event_version: Note: this computer's code version ({mine}) differs from the portal's ({theirs}); updating both to the same version (git pull) is safer.
cli.worker.event_offline: Cannot reach the portal at {server} ({reason}); retrying automatically.
cli.worker.event_reported: {run} finished: {status}; the result was sent to the portal.
cli.worker.event_abandoned: The portal took {run} back (for example after losing contact); this result is not reported.
cli.worker.event_report_failed: The result could not be sent to the portal: {reason}
cli.worker.invite_help: Pair using an invitation from the portal's Devices page (the whole rpa://pair?… line, or the code together with --server); the token it gives is saved in the working folder, so you do not need it again.
cli.worker.no_server: The portal's address is required: give it with --server, for example http://192.168.1.10:8081.
cli.worker.paired: Paired as {name} ({device}); the token is saved in {path} (readable only by you).
cli.worker.pair_offline: Cannot reach the portal at {server} ({reason}): check that rpa serve was started with --worker-port and that this computer can reach that address.
cli.worker.invite_empty: The invitation is empty: paste the whole invitation line from the Devices page.
cli.worker.invite_format: This is not an invitation: paste the whole rpa://pair?… line from the Devices page, or just the code together with --server.
cli.worker.invite_server: The server URL is not valid: it should look like http://192.168.1.10:8081 (with only the code, give it with --server).
cli.worker.invite_app: The invitation names an unknown app: create a new one on the Devices page.
